references.text: Warning against making a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, as this will become a snare for the Israelites
Prohibition against serving foreign gods because it will be a snare for God's people
Warning against being caught in a trap by following other peoples' gods
Joshua's warning that the remaining nations will become a snare if Israel mixes with them
Fulfillment of the warning: the gods of the remaining nations became a snare for Israel
Israel's idolatry with the idols of neighboring peoples became a snare for them
The prohibition against making a covenant with the Canaanites and their gods, which leads to this warning
The reason for driving out the peoples is that they should not teach Israel to sin against the Lord
Complementary text: Exodus 34:15 explains the concrete mechanism (marriage and meals) that makes foreigners a 'snare' as mentioned in 23:33.
Interconnected within the same chapter: 23:24 provides the solution (extermination) to avoid the danger described in 23:33.
Strong thematic parallel: Numbers 33:55 describes the consequence (thorns/刺) of not driving out the nations, which in Exodus 23:33 is described as a 'snare'.
